findings.title: Mirror lake flashes black for 1-2 frames after every render-size change (adaptive scale step, window or phone-toolbar resize) at T1
findings.evidence: qc5/flash2_lane_flash.png vs qc5/flash2_lane_before.png: the whole lake (y ~455-766 outside floes and rocks) is black, with a row of white dashes at y ~565. Lake band means (qc5/flash_lane.log, qc5/flash2_lane.log; canvas read in a rAF after the engine's render): 165 -> 60.45 on an adaptive step 648->576 with no input; 164 -> 56.22 / 56.27 on window 766->760; 163 -> 60.31-60.84 on 760->766; 164 -> 59.33 on scale 0.85->1 via resize(). The dark frames are exactly the frames with lakeMirror.reused = 1 or 2 right after LakeMirror.setSize. THREE.WebGLRenderTarget.setSize disposes the target, then LakeMirror.render() reuses it because the camera has not moved, so the water samples an empty mirror. Baseline under the same events: at most 2 levels (qc5/flash_base.log). Visitors run with the adaptive scale unlocked; only the captures pin ?scale=1, so the builder's captures could not see this.
findings.fix_hint: In LakeMirror.setSize, when the size actually changes, invalidate the reuse (this.lastPos.set(Infinity, 0, 0); this.reused = 0) so the very next frame renders the mirror. Optionally render it straight away from HeroEngine.resize(). Re-check with WORK/judge1/tools/resizeflash.mjs: no lake-band frame below ~150 across window and scale changes, at T1 and on the phone tier.

findings.title: The mirror lake erases the floe and iceberg reflection columns and reads as a CG ripple texture; lake region means fall outside +-3 at every clock time
findings.evidence: crops3/q00_floesR_x2_BLR.png (base / lane / F000, 2x): F000 and the baseline have a bright column under every far floe; the lane has none, not even under the small floe at ~(1180,495). Water under the right floes (940,500,500,60): column structure col F000 21.8, base 14.6, lane 9.0 (t200: 7.8); horizontal-line energy gy F000 1.85, base 2.00, lane 4.63. Near-water detail gx (500,600,400,60): F000 2.50, lane 0.79. Same in the hold (crops3/p06_lake_BLR.png vs F420) and the pointer views (eg2/crops/edgeL_x2_left.png, edgeR_x2_right.png). Lake boxes, lane minus base at t100/200/300: lake_mid_left -13.2/-3.4/-4.1, lake_near_centre +3.4/+9.7/+5.9, lake_right -3.0/-7.5/-7.6, far_floes_right -4.4/-3.5/-2.5. ?envlake=plate gives +-1.5. Root cause (qc5/diag_lakeR_lane_nospread_flat_base.png): with the bump off the floes and the iceberg are crisply in the mirror target. mirrorTex() then spreads them over one symmetric textureGrad box of 3.46 sigma in elevation (fine octaves with sig ~ 2*s.z*1.4, plus the uLakeFar far-field 0.05 rad from 15-45 m), which averages the thin floe reflections into the sky.
findings.fix_hint: Keep the mirror for robustness, but model the Cycles bump as a vertical streak below each reflected feature instead of a wide symmetric blur. Take several taps along the elevation toward and below the reflected point, weighted by the slope distribution. Narrow or drop the far-field spread for low-elevation, near-waterline features: it was added only to wash out the massif foot. Fit the result to F000's column contrast (col ~20 under the right floes, gy ~2) and the lake boxes to within +-3. Until it passes, ship ?envlake=plate (the step-1 plate lake on the baked environment) as the default; it already passes E-G1.

findings.title: Frame time at T1 is +12-15 % over the baseline whenever the camera moves (the mirror renders every frame); +6.8 % with the camera still
findings.evidence: Paired synchronous timing, lane/base median ratio (perf/pair_rest_default.txt, pair_rest_rate1.txt, pair_hold_rate1_b.txt, pair_hold_rate1.txt): camera still 1.068; ?envmirrorrate=1, i.e. any camera motion (cursor orbit, hover dolly, hold dolly, release, intro), rest 1.121 and hold 1.124 at load 5.86 (1.154 at load 11.3). The builder's HANDOFF also reports 1.12-1.16 without reuse. perf_probe, 6 interleaved pairs (perf/probe.txt): medians inconclusive under contention, but the worst frame is lane 83.4 ms vs base 66.8 ms. The extra cost makes the adaptive scale step down, which triggers the blocker flash, and bigger frames mean bigger per-frame ring steps in the hold the user is complaining about.
findings.fix_hint: Cheapen the moving-camera mirror pass. Options: single-sided raster in the mirror pass (the builder measured ~2 ms for double-sided); drop small rocks and the far-side geometry the reflection never shows; a smaller T1 target while moving (e.g. 0.5 x 0.35); or render the mirror at half rate during motion with the previous target reprojected. Re-measure with paired timing and ?envmirrorrate=1 until it is <= 1.10.

summary:
ENV lane, judge1 (attempt 3, resumed from the 09:07 cut-off). I used fresh pinned-clock captures of the lane lab on :5174, which I started and have stopped, against the baseline on :5173 (untouched) and the reference frames. Every image cited was inspected at full resolution or zoomed. The baked environment itself is good: outside the lake every rest box is within +-0.5 of the projected baseline, it reads the same from all 10 pointer spots and the full sweep, nothing doubles, and there is one wisp everywhere. The way back passes (E-G4 <= 0.48, the same as the baseline's own dither repeat). Assets are 2.54 MB and the typecheck is clean.

The new mirror lake fails the lane:
- BLOCKER: the whole lake flashes black for 1-2 frames after any render-size change (adaptive scale steps, window or phone-toolbar resizes). LakeMirror reuses a target that setSize just disposed. Proof: qc5/flash2_lane_flash.png. The fix is a one-line reuse invalidation in setSize.
- MAJOR: the lake drops every floe and iceberg reflection column that F000 and F420 show and reads as regular CG wave lines. Lake boxes fall outside +-3 at every clock time. The cause is the wide symmetric elevation spread in mirrorTex(): with the bump off, the floes are crisply in the mirror. ?envlake=plate passes E-G1 now.
- MAJOR: frame time is +12-15 % whenever the camera moves (+6.8 % with the camera still) in paired timing. MAIN's perf_probe (6 pairs) was too contended to resolve 10 %.
- MINOR: deterministic bright specks and notches on the ridge, and aliased skyline edges.

The user's hold priority (decision 6), checked as a regression: ENV does not touch ring code, and live presses show the same behaviour on both builds. In a 20 s hold B moves 2.4 deg/s and D 0.6 deg/s with 13-14 spin sign flips, C crawls, and the outer rings hit the 45 deg per-frame clamp on release. The user's complaint is real on the baseline; it is for the HOLD lane to fix, and ENV adds nothing to it except frame time.
